issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a terrorism trauma, sexual-violence comments as a primary trigger is hard to reconcile unless the index event also involved sexual assault or closely related content; nothing else in the profile supports that connection.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: The appraisal of betrayal by a trusted person is difficult to fit with terrorism as the trauma type unless there was a clear interpersonal betrayal component; the rest of the selected items describe loss of control, helplessness, avoidance, dissociation, and substance use rather than interpersonal betrayal.

vignette: Raj, a 37-year-old South Asian male and psychologist, has been struggling with PTSD symptoms since he witnessed a terrorist attack two years ago. The incident left him feeling deeply shaken, particularly by the sense of loss of control and the terrifying auditory cues that accompanied it. Raj vividly recalls the night-time setting, the sudden darkness, and the deafening gunshot noises that shattered his sense of security. Since then, Raj has found himself increasingly wary of these triggers. Nighttime and the dark have become sources of profound anxiety for him; he often wakes up startled in the middle of the night, drenched in sweat, reliving fragments of the attack. The sound of sirens or fireworks, even if faint, can instantly plunge him back into that harrowing moment. This heightened sensitivity to triggers has led Raj to adopt several maladaptive strategies to cope with his distress. To avoid the overwhelming sense of helplessness he feels when confronted with these cues, Raj increasingly turns to alcohol and medication. These substances provide a temporary escape from his traumatic memories and the pervasive fear that grips him at night. He also retreats into fantasy worlds, often getting lost in daydreams where he has control over events and can protect himself and others. However, this escapism has begun to affect his work as a psychologist; he finds it difficult to focus on his patients and is often preoccupied during sessions. Raj's maladaptive strategies have compounded his negative appraisals about the world and himself. He now believes that the world is an inherently dangerous place where bad things happen without warning, and there is little he can do to prevent them. The person he has become feels unrecognizable to him-a stark contrast from the confident professional he once was. This self-perception as helpless and vulnerable further fuels his reliance on alcohol and fantasy escape, creating a cycle that seems impossible to break. Moreover, Raj's substance use and escapism have begun to strain his relationship with his wife. She has noticed changes in his behavior but is unsure how to help him or even approach the topic without triggering another episode of intense anxiety. The mounting tension at home, coupled with the impact on his work, has pushed Raj to seek professional help. Raj's current state reveals a man grappling with overwhelming fears and a sense of lost identity. He is most afraid that he will never regain control over his life or be able to manage his symptoms without falling back into harmful coping mechanisms. At the same time, he holds onto hope for reclaiming his former self and finding effective ways to navigate the world again, free from the constant shadow of fear and helplessness. The trauma has left Raj with a profound sense that the world is perilous, making it difficult for him to trust his surroundings or even himself. His maladaptive strategies have become a lifeline but are also perpetuating the cycle of negative beliefs and reinforcing the very triggers he seeks to avoid. The urgency in seeking help stems from his deep-seated hope that with proper support, he can break this cycle and regain a sense of control over his life.
